_comment: Context window sizes per model id, resolved at READ time by `cli/cost.py`.
This deliberately does not populate `turn_norm.context_window`. That
column means 'the harness reported this' — Codex fills it from
`info.model_context_window`, Claude never does. Writing a lookup into it
would destroy the measured-versus-inferred distinction the `~` marker
depends on, and would silently change the meaning of historical rows.
So the lookup stays here, at the read surface, and every value it
produces is marked inferred.
MATCHING: exact id first, then longest matching prefix. Real ids carry
release-date suffixes that the table should not have to chase —
`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` resolves via the `claude-haiku-4-5` entry.
Longest-prefix rather than any-prefix so a future `claude-opus-5-1` entry
wins over `claude-opus-5` instead of tying with it.
A model string in a Claude transcript carries no window suffix — a 1M
session and a 200K session both read `claude-opus-5`. Where a model has a
long-context variant, `long_window` and `long_threshold` express that:
context observed above the threshold must be the long variant, anything
below is assumed standard. That assumption overstates percentages for an
unidentified long-window session, which is why two better sources are
tried first (see `_resolve_window`): the statusline's exact record, and
`preTokens` at an auto-compaction in that same session.
A model absent from this table reports its window as unknown and its
percentage is suppressed rather than guessed. An honest blank beats a
confident wrong number in a tool whose purpose is measurement — and it is
the signal that this file needs a new entry. Deliberately absent today:
`<synthetic>` and `codex-auto-review`, which are not models and have no
window, and a NULL model, which is not a lookup key at all.
Verified 2026-08-15 against every model id present in the local corpus.
